subject: Request for Clarification: Inference Fabric Zones, Egress Allowlist and Adversary Walkthrough
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@orionbank.com>

Cc: Orion Bank SecOps <infra-security@orionbank.com>
Date: 2026-09-14 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: RFI: Clarify inference fabric zones and allowed egress

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. As we work through Orion's vendor risk review I have a couple of follow-ups specific to network isolation and egress controls for the inference service you demonstrated (our reviewers called it the "inference fabric"). Could you please provide clarifications and any supporting artifacts for the items below? We aim to close this RFI before our AMR on 2026-09-21.

1) Logical topology: a concise diagram showing control plane, serving nodes, tenant boundaries, and any sidecars or proxies in-path.
2) Egress flow: where outbound model downloads, telemetry, and webhooks exit to the internet (e.g., NAT gateway, egress proxy, peered VPC), and how allowlists are applied per-tenant.
3) Credential scope: KMS/HSM usage for keys, who holds keys, and whether customer-managed keys are supported.
4) Threat scenarios: a short adversary walk-through for a lateral movement/exfiltration scenario originating from a compromised customer model or VM.
5) Evidence: any control evidence (network ACLs, audit log retention, bastion session logs) you can share or redacted screenshots.

If you have a single consolidated packet that's easiest for auditors, but we can also accept smaller artifacts. Can you confirm an ETA? Ideally we would have something by 2026-09-16.

Best,
Marta

Marta Lopez
Lead, Vendor Security Reviews
Orion Bank

Subject: Re: RFI: Clarify inference fabric zones and allowed egress

Hi Marta —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached are three artifacts that should address each item:
- inference_fabric_zone_diagram_v2.pdf (logical topology + legend)
- egress_policy_matrix.xlsx (per-tenant egress patterns and allowlist controls)
- attack_path_playbook_v1.md (short adversary walk-throughs and mitigations)

High-level summary below; the attachments have the detail. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through.

Logical topology (summary):
- Control plane: a customer-managed or Redwood-managed control plane option. For hosted customers, the control plane coordinates model versions, routing, and telemetry; control plane endpoints are region-scoped and accessible over TLS with mTLS to customer connectors.
- Serving plane: workload isolation is enforced by dedicated tenant namespaces running on our inference cluster. Each tenant gets logically isolated VPC segments and a set of sidecars for token policy and KV cache mediation.
- Sidecars & proxies: every serving replica has a local sidecar proxy that enforces egress policy, request provenance tagging, and rate limiting. Sidecars run with least privilege and forward telemetry to our central collectors over an internal TLS mesh.

Egress controls & allowlisting: 
- Outbound model pulls: model artifacts are pulled from curated registries via an egress broker service that enforces TLS, signature checking, and a downloadable-artifact allowlist. For Dedicated and Private deployments customers can opt to provide an on-prem registry.
- Tenant-scoped allowlists: per-tenant egress policies are maintained in the policy database. Egress is brokered through a NAT/eBPF gateway that applies allowlists and tags flows with tenant IDs. Changes require authenticated API calls and are recorded in audit logs.
- Telemetry and webhooks: outbound telemetry and webhook endpoints also pass through an application-level proxy and require allowlist approval; webhook destinations are rate-limited and validated against known DNS/IP lists.

Credential management & audit: 
- KMS: we support Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed KMS (BYOK). Keys for tenant encryption at rest and in-transit are stored in HSM-backed KMS; key use is audited.
- Audit retention: per-contract log retention configurable; default 13 months for audit trails, 90 days for detailed debug traces. Bastion session recordings for operator actions are retained as part of the audit bundle.

Adversary walk-through (short):
- Scenario: attacker obtains a container-level exploit on a compromised third-party model runner.
- Containment: tenant namespace isolation + egress broker prevents arbitrary outbound connections; sidecar enforces allowlist so attacker cannot directly exfiltrate to unknown endpoints.
- Detection & response: anomalous KV cache access and unexpected outbound attempts trigger alerts to SOC; we have playbooks for snapshot-and-failover to immutable serving images and forensic capture.

Evidence & artifacts: included in the zip: network diagrams, sample audit logs (redacted), and our egress policy matrix. For sensitive screenshots we can produce redacted PDFs.

ETA: we can provide the attached packet now; if you need an additional dedicated evidence packet for auditors (signed attestations, SOC2 artifact references) we can produce that by 2026-09-20.

Regards,

Priya Natarajan

Priya —

Thanks for the thorough packet, this should cover most questions. A couple of quick asks before we send the final bundle to Marta's team:

- Can we add a short paragraph in the playbook about KV cache exposure risks and how we rotate cache keys / evict namespaces on suspicious activity? Orion specifically flagged "cache leakage" as a high concern.
- Please include the model-pull supply chain note: which registries are allowed by default and how signed-model verification is enforced end-to-end (artifact provenance).
- Does the audit bundle include a recent egress policy change log (with ticket refs) so they can verify change control? If not, add an anonymized extract.

If you want, I can draft the KV cache paragraph and paste into attack_path_playbook_v1.md and push an updated attachment.

-Karthik
